5574814314775384168: "High Mountains and Flowing Waters" is one of China's top ten ancient musical pieces. Originally a single composition, it was divided into two separate qin pieces, "High Mountains" and "Flowing Waters," after the Tang Dynasty. The score first appeared in the Ming Dynasty's "Shen Qi Mi Pu" (Mysterious and Secret Notation). The phrase "high mountains and flowing waters" originates from "Liezi · Tang Wen," which tells the legend of Bo Ya, a master of the qin, and Zhong Ziqi, a discerning listener. When Bo Ya played with his heart set on high mountains, Zhong Ziqi exclaimed, "How magnificent! Towering like Mount Tai." When his heart turned to flowing waters, Zhong Ziqi said, "How splendid! Vast like the rivers." Whatever Bo Ya envisioned, Zhong Ziqi would grasp it. After Ziqi's death, Bo Ya believed no one in the world could understand his music anymore, so he broke his qin and severed its strings, never playing again for the rest of his life.
